

Same file, or `store/reviewthreads.go` if `reviews.go` is long.

- `OpenThread(tx, now, reviewID, in, actorID, taskID, sessionID, eventID)`:
  `reviewID` may be 0 for a bare note (WL-REQ-1319). An anchor is one of
  two shapes. A range anchor (`Version`, `ByteStart`, `ByteEnd`, `Quote`
  set) is validated per Decisions against the stored Markdown of the named
  version (`rule_versions.body` for a rule, `docs.body` for a plan or a
  spec's template; a range on a spec is first mapped by Task 7); a mismatch
  between the range and `Quote` is `ErrInvalidInput` naming the first
  differing byte, and `DocAnchor` is derived from the range through the
  section map `internal/designdoc` already computes. A section anchor
  (`DocAnchor` set, the four range fields zero) is stored with `version`,
  `byte_start`, `byte_end` and `quote` null (WL-REQ-1667), and is refused
  when the section does not exist on the document. A review thread
  (`reviewID != 0`) must carry a range anchor. The first message is the
  thread's body with `role = author` when `actorID == reviewAuthor(...)`,
  else `reviewer`. `seq` is the review's `next_seq` for a review thread
  and 1 for a bare note's first message. `intent_classifier` and
  `intent_confidence` are written null (the client stated the intent,
  WL-REQ-1885). `intent = question` emits `wl:ReviewQuestionAsked`.
- `ReplyThread(tx, now, threadID, body, actorID, eventID)`: refused on a
  `resolved` or `obsolete` thread. `seq` continues the review's `next_seq`,
  or the thread's own count for a bare note. The first reply with `role =
  author` on a `question` thread emits `wl:ReviewQuestionAnswered`; the
  store returns `firstAuthorReply bool` and the question's `created_at` so
  Task 10 can observe `question_latency_seconds`.
- `ResolveThread(tx, now, threadID, actorID, status, eventID)`: `resolved`
  or `obsolete`; emits `wl:ReviewThreadResolved` with `wl:threadStatus`.
- `ThreadsForSubject(ctx, doc, rule, version, section, status)`: bare notes
  and review threads on one document or rule, `obsolete` included, narrowed
  to a version, a section or a status when given, oldest first. This is what
  the WL-REQ-1323 thread-list routes serve (Task 10).
- The fold: a second migration pair
  `deploy/base/migrations/NEW-doc-notes-fold.{up,down}.sql`, landed in the
  same PR as the store change so `TestDocNote` is green at every commit on
  `main`. Up copies the notes, carrying each note's id through a temporary
  column so the message join is exact:

```sql
ALTER TABLE review_threads ADD COLUMN fold_note_id bigint;
INSERT INTO review_threads
    (doc_id, doc_anchor, raised_by_task, raised_by_session,
     intent, status, author_id, created_at, fold_note_id)
SELECT n.doc_id, n.anchor, n.task_id,
       (SELECT s.id FROM agent_sessions s
         WHERE s.id = CASE WHEN n.session_id ~ '^[0-9]{1,18}$'
                           THEN n.session_id::bigint END),
       'note', 'open', COALESCE(n.created_by, 'worklode'), n.created_at, n.id
  FROM doc_notes n ORDER BY n.id;
-- The note's text is its first message; seq is per thread for a bare note.
INSERT INTO review_messages (thread_id, seq, actor_id, role, body, created_at)
SELECT t.id, 1, t.author_id, 'reviewer', n.body, n.created_at
  FROM review_threads t JOIN doc_notes n ON n.id = t.fold_note_id;
ALTER TABLE review_threads DROP COLUMN fold_note_id;
DROP TABLE doc_notes;
```

  The `CASE` is what keeps the cast off a non-numeric `session_id`:
  Postgres does not promise short-circuit evaluation of a `WHERE`
  conjunction. Down recreates `doc_notes` from bare note threads that have
  `doc_anchor` and no range (`session_id` as text, `body` from the first
  message) and drops them from `review_threads` and `review_messages`.
- `AddDocNote`/`ListDocNotes` (`internal/store/docnotes.go`) now write and
  read `review_threads` with `review_id IS NULL` plus one `review_messages`
  row. `lode doc note <ref>#sec-N` stores `doc_anchor = sec-N` and nothing
  else of the anchor (WL-REQ-1667): no version, no byte range, no quote, so
  editing the section never makes a note `obsolete`. `model.DocNote`'s JSON
  does not change. The `doc.note_added` event stays as it is.

First store test:

```go
func TestThreadLifecycle(t *testing.T) {
    // open review over a spec; reviewer a opens a question on bytes of rule R's text.
    th, _ := store.OpenThread(tx, now, r.ID, model.OpenThreadInput{
        Anchor: model.ReviewAnchor{Rule: R.ID, Version: 1, ByteStart: 10, ByteEnd: 18, Quote: "the gate"},
        Intent: "question", Body: "why two lanes?"}, "a", "", "", ev)
    // want: status open; DocAnchor derived "sec-2"; one message role reviewer, seq 1; event wl:ReviewQuestionAsked.
    // owner replies → firstAuthorReply true, event wl:ReviewQuestionAnswered.
    // second owner reply → firstAuthorReply false, no second event.
    // resolve by a → status resolved, event wl:ReviewThreadResolved.
    // reply after resolve → ErrInvalidInput.
    // Quote "the gat" with the same range → ErrInvalidInput.
    // ByteStart inside a multibyte character → ErrInvalidInput.
    // review thread with a section anchor only → ErrInvalidInput.
    // `lode doc note` on sec-2 → bare thread with doc_anchor sec-2 and null version/range/quote.
    // ThreadsForSubject(doc, 0, 0, "sec-2", "") → 2 rows.
}
```
